prompt: Hypothetical. In the order window you enter a buy of 10 shares at Rs 250. You do not submit it. What is the order value before charges?
solution: Order value = 10 multiplied by Rs 250 = Rs 2,500, before charges. Check: Rs 2,500 divided by 10 shares = Rs 250 a share.

prompt: Which statement about the Kite demo is correct?

options.text: The demo is a paper-trading account that records your ideas.
The demo uses dummy data and is for practice with the screens only.
The demo shows real market prices for paper trading.
The demo is the same thing as a paper-trading account.

explanations.a: The demo is not a record of your ideas. Paper trading means keeping that record. Check Zerodha's exact wording. [VERIFY: exact wording on Zerodha support]
explanations.c: Demo data is dummy data. Its prices are not real market prices.
explanations.d: The demo and a paper-trading account are different things. Do not treat the demo as a record of your decisions.

options.text: Reports and statements, as a back-office area

explanations.a: Orders are entered in the order window. Console is not the place to enter an order. Check Zerodha's Console help. [VERIFY: Console contents]
explanations.c: Alerts are a separate feature. Console is a back-office area for records and reports.
explanations.d: Live chart prices are shown on the chart, not in Console.

prompt: Hypothetical. A student says: 'The demo shows real prices, so I can practise paper trading with it and trust my results.' What is the best reply?

options.text: Correct. Demo prices are real market prices.
The demo uses dummy data and is for practice with the screens. Results from it do not show trading skill.
Correct, as long as you use the demo every day.
Wrong. Paper trading needs a live account.

explanations.a: The demo uses dummy data. Its prices are not real market prices.
explanations.c: Using the demo often does not change dummy data. Familiarity with the screens is not evidence of trading skill.
explanations.d: Paper trading means practising with pretend money and keeping a record. It does not need a live account.

prompt: Spot the mistake. A student writes: 'I will post a cropped screenshot. The name and client ID are cut out, so the balance is safe to show.' Which part is the mistake?

options.text: I will post a cropped screenshot.
The name and client ID are cut out.
So the balance is safe to show.

explanations.a: Cropping before you share is the correct step.
explanations.b: Removing the name and client ID is correct. The rule also covers balances, so the balance must be removed too.
